title.narrative: International Federation for Human Rights, FIDH, core support 2025-2027
International Federation for Human Rights, FIDH, kärnstöd 2025-2027

description.narrative:
Core support to International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH) 2025 - 2027.
FIDH is a federation of 192 human rights organisations from 117 countries. FIDH works for the promotion of human rights as expressed in the Universal declaration of Human Rights and the other central human rights conventions. Human Rights are a precondition for economic development and equitable growth.

Kärnstöd till FIDH, International Federation for Human Rights, för perioden 2025- 2027.
FIDH är en federation bestående av 192 MR-organisationer från 117 länder. FIDH verkar för att skydda och upprätthålla de mänskliga rättigheterna såsom de uttrycks i FN's deklaration om de mänskliga rättigheterna och de övriga centrala konventionerna för mänskliga rättigheter. FIDH riktar sig både mot ansvarsbärare och rättighetsbärare. Mänskliga rättigheter är en förutsättning för ekonomisk utveckling och jämlikt välstånd.

The two goals of the FIDH Strategy 2030
1. Strengthen FIDH to bolster the Global Human Rights movement, and
2. Promote human rights for all by addressing present and future challenges
Both goals are similar to the goals of the previous strategy but now also reflect gender as a cross-cutting priority and not as a separate priority area.
Goal 1, Strategic priorities and objectives
(i) Strengthen the mobilization, representativeness and accountability of FIDH's governance
- The members of the International Board better reflect diversity (including youth and women/non-binary) and are empowered to carry out their functions
- The International Board is informed and supported by the views of experts
- The representatives sent to the triennal World Congress illustrate the diversity of the movement
- FIDH World Congress is an increased opportunity to enhance the impact of key activities and ownership of the Federation beyond the representatives who attend the Congress
(ii) Revitalize FIDH's membership
- The inclusion of new member organisations into the network is facilitated
- Member organisations have a better knowledge of the work, expertise, and thematic actions of each other
- More organisations are committed to an approach that is more inclusive of a plurality of gender identities
(iii) Increase the visibility of FIDH's work
- FIDH communication is increasingly part of the strategy to influence decision-makers
- FIDH is gaining recognition from a wider public, beyond its usual targets
- The federative aspect of the FIDH's identity is enhances through joint communication actions
Goal 2, strategic priorities and objectives
(i) Protect and empower human rights defenders (HRDs)
- HRDs escape repression and are better protected
- Actors who are levers of change, including national authorities, foreign diplomats, regional and international intergovernmental institutions and, in some cases, companies and judicial authorities, adopt public positions and take action for the protection of HRDs
- HRDs are technically and strategically equipped to deal with threats and to fight back
- The work of local human rights organisations is enabled and can continue through the awarding of institutional protection and capacity building grants
- Trends in threats, attacks, criminalization, harassment against HRDs and violations of HRDs' rights are identified, documented and denounced
- The responsibility of the perpetrators of violations of the rights of HRDs and NGOs is established, and those responsible of the violations are held accountable
- The adoption of consultation frameworks, declarations, resolutions, and political, administrative, and legislative measures favorable to HRDs and their NGOs is promoted
- National legislations, policies or mechanisms that guarantee and protect the role and action of HRDs and NGOs is advocated
- Media, public opinion, and national authorities are better sensitized about the role of HRDs
(ii) Fostering an enabling environment for effective and inclusive democracy
- The authorities are hampered in their repressive, arbitrary and anti-democratic initiatives (including the use of mass surveillance and opinion manipulation technologies)
- Policy and legislative reforms that increase civic space and enables the exercise of fundamental rights and freedoms (primarily freedom of expression, association, and peaceful assembly) are adopted
- Enhanced spaces of dialogue between civil society and public authorities at the national level on policy reforms and public policies.
- Counter-narratives are developed to oppose those who aim at delegitimize civil society
- Attempts by states to undermine democratic checks and balances and the rule of law, particularly judicial independence, are denounce with a view to ensuring accountability
- States are held accountable for breaches of the rule of law and human rights violations linked to large-scale corruption and misuse of public funds and resources
- Progress are made to address inequalities and to ensure non-discriminations in law and practice
- Respect for civil, political, economic, social, and cultural rights is promoted in economic and financial policies
- Violence in periods of social or political instability and electoral periods is addressed
- Authorities are alerted about the need to ensure that security measures, including those adopted in the fight against terrorism, and even in emergency states, do not take priority over the respect of human rights, human life, and human dignity
- Progress towards universal abolition of the death penalty is made
(iii) Promote international justice as a pillar for the rule of law
- The facts and responsibilities for the most serious crimes are documented and established
- Integrated strategies to activate different and complementary accountability mechanisms are developed by civil society
- Legal proceedings initiated by FIDH with the participation of victims and their representatives
- Victims and affected communities have improved knowledge of the procedure and are better able to claim their rights
- Victims' access to justice mechanisms is improved
- National and/or hybrid accountability mechanisms are strengthened and made more effective
- Adequate universal jurisdiction legal frameworks and practices are in place
- Independent investigative mechanisms collecting and analyzing evidence of the most serious crimes are provided information by civil society
- The ICC undertakes meaningful investigations, prosecution, outreach strategies and effective implementation of victim's rights
- An effective cooperation and complementarity between accountability mechanisms is promoted
- A narrative reminding the fundamentals of the fight against impunity is developed and shared
- The issues of justice and the fight against impunity are brought closer to the daily lives of decision makers
- The fight against impunity is back on the political agenda of decision-makers
(iv) Promote respect for human rights and the environment by economic actors
- Binding rules for companies aimed at better prevention and protection against human rights abuses and negative environmental impacts are adopted at the UN, EU and the national level
- The right to a healthy environment is recognized and fulfilled by states and international organisations
- Free trade agreements include human rights and environmental protection clauses and participatory dispute settlement mechanisms
- Judicial and extrajudicial actors aimed at establishing the responsibility of economic actors for human rights and environmental violations and for their contribution to climate change are initiated and/or continued
- Advocacy spaces with economic actors that can influence the protection of human rights and the environmental are created or maintained
- Member and partner organisations know and implement a methodology for documenting violations linked to economic activities, known as "Community Based Human Rights Impact Assessment (COBHRIA)
- Cross-regional strategic discussion and mobilization spaces are created and maintained
- Civil-society and affected communities influence the implementation of international human rights obligations by economic actors
(v) Promote women's rights and combat discrimination and violence based on sexual orientation and gender identity (cross-cutting)
- Normative protection against SGBV is increased an implemented
- Survivors have access to justice and appropriate public services
- SGBV crimes are increasingly recognized in judicial proceedings
- The influence of anti-rights and anti-gender movements is exposed and challenged
- Laws criminalizing homosexuality are challenged
- States are urged to respect sexual and reproductive health rights
- Member and partner organisations are sensitized in the rhetoric of the anti-rights and anti-gender movements and develop strategies to respond to them
(vi) Strengthen leverages and international mechanisms for the protection of human rights (cross-cutting)
- HRDs and human rights NGOs' elaboration of collective mobilization is facilitated
- Information on human rights situation is used for advocacy purposes at international level and is widely disseminated
- Interaction between HRDs and human rights NGOs with intergovernmental mechanisms, third countries, corporations and other levers of influence is facilitated
- International human rights protection mechanisms echo the demands and recommendations of HRDs and human rights NGOs
- New levers of influence in the field of human rights are consolidated and strengthened
- International mechanisms to protect civilian populations in situations of armed conflict and crises are triggered
